notes: A clean three-rung courier quest and the easiest page in the batch. Both sub-bullets are the key items you receive, not actions, so each is folded into its parent step as evidence rather than becoming a rung of its own. Neither hand-over is a trade: Weapons order and Weapons receipt are KEY items, which never sit in inventory and cannot be dragged onto an NPC, so steps 2 and 3 are conversations that require you to be holding the key item -- recorded as items with kind 'ki'. Both key items resolve (97 and 98) and both are unique, so the ladder has real evidence on its first two rungs and the third is reached only while holding the receipt. The Elm Staff is the header's Reward and is deliberately not evidence anywhere.

steps.note: at the weapon shop; the page's 'after completing Father and Son' is the Previous gate restated, not an action
the traveling merchant, near the lake. 'Bring' is a conversation, not a trade -- a key item cannot be traded.

notes: Three bullets, three real steps. 'Quadav Charm' is an ordinary ITEM (id 495), not a key item -- the ki table has no such name -- so it is tradeable and step 3 is a genuine trade. The Coruscant rosary is the header's Reward and therefore is NOT evidence on step 3; the only observable rung is step 2, where killing De'Vyu Headhunter puts the charm in your bag. 'Quest Reqs: Bastok Mission 4-1, or San d'Oria Mission 4-1, or Windurst Mission 4-1' is a three-way OR over MISSIONS: prev is an AND-list of quests, so listing all three would gate the quest on doing all three nations, and listing one would be a guess. It is dropped and flagged instead. The wiki gives the headhunter's spawn as a two-cell range (I-9/I-10) and that is kept verbatim rather than picked apart.

steps.note: the charm is the drop, so the mob carries the marker and the step target is none
the Coruscant rosary he gives back is the reward, not evidence

notes:
A Voidwatch storyline link with an EMPTY Start field, so the giver is read out of bullet 1: a Voidwatch Officer. That is the whole quest -- bullet 2 is the outcome ('receiving the item ends this quest and begins the next'), not a second rung, and adding one would put a marker after the quest has already closed. The honest problem is the marker: 'Voidwatch Officer' is on the normaliser's AMBIGUOUS_NPCS list, where a resolved zone is MANDATORY, and the page names no zone at all -- 'any present-day Voidwatch Officer' is exactly the point, there is one in every major city. So the zone stays null, the entry will be dropped rather than marked on every officer in Vana'diel, and the quest keeps its rung and loses its arrow. Inventing a city to make the marker appear would be a guess dressed as data. Evidence is real though: the Voidwatch alarum (ki 2048) is granted here and is not in the Reward field, which is empty. Fame 'Wings of the Goddess' is an expansion name that leaked into the fame column and gates nothing, so region is null with raw kept.

notes: All three rungs are the same NPC in the same spot, which the runtime folds to one marker, and the readiness look-ahead is what makes the ladder worth having: holding three Shell Bugs is what says 'go back to Ronan'. Bullet 2 packs sourcing and the trade into one sentence, but the sourcing half names no zone and no monster -- 'Quadavs or the Auction House' is a family and a shop, not targets -- so splitting out an obtain rung would wedge an unmarkable, unmarked step between two Ronan steps and buy nothing. It stays one trade carrying Shell Bug x3. The sub-bullet about the Green Thumb Moogle and a Baby eft memento is a third sourcing route, not a step. Bullet 3's zone-out-and-back-in is a real requirement and a real gap: nothing in the packets reports that you zoned, so the rung exists but only the quest completing can retire it. The Monk's Headgear is the Reward and is not evidence.

steps.note: all three at once. Sources are Quadavs, the auction house, or the Green Thumb Moogle with a Baby eft memento -- none of them a place this can point at.
you must leave the zone and come back before he will finish it; zoning is not observable

notes: One rung, not three. Bullets 1 and 2 are the same conversation with the same moogle -- you talk to him and choose to spend the merits inside that one dialogue -- so they merge; there is no observable state between them and no second place to stand. Bullet 3 is not a step at all: it is a stray template the prepass could not render ('tpl:math357') followed by advice that says outright the skill is 'not necessary to complete this quest'. The Heart of the bushin resolves (ki 2059) but is the header's Reward, so it proves the quest is over rather than that the step is done, and it is not used as evidence -- which leaves this ladder with none, correctly. 'Nomad Moogle' is an ambiguous name that needs a zone to survive the normaliser; Ru'Lude Gardens (243) supplies it, and v1's index already marks nomad moogle at z=243 for the sibling quests. Fifteen merit points are a currency, not inventory, so the item requirement gates nothing observable; the level 96 gate is real and kept.

steps.note: the one standing near Maat. Fifteen merit points are spent in the same conversation, which is why bullets 1 and 2 are one rung.

notes: A one-line Mog Garden quest and genuinely a one-step ladder: trade a Cotton Thread and it is over. Chacharoon is named only in the Description as the reason for the errand -- he is not who you interact with and he gets no step. Mog Garden resolves as a zone (280), so the trade has a real place even though the page gives no grid, and Mog Garden has no grid to give. The header's 'Quest Reqs: Cotton Thread' is an ITEM requirement sitting in the wrong column, which is why Item Reqs is empty; it is the same thread as the trade and is not double-counted. The Lamb memento, Roast Mutton and the Monster Rearing unlock are rewards.

steps.note: the cutscene and the completion both follow from this single trade

notes: Four bullets, two steps. Bullets 1 and 2 are directions to a man who is standing in the zone the step already names -- 'zone at (C-7) in Northern San d'Oria' and 'you should be in a watchtower in West Ronfaure now' -- so they are the route to step 1, not rungs. Making a travel step out of them would put a West Ronfaure marker immediately before a West Ronfaure marker. Bullet 4 is a second, real visit to the same NPC and stays its own rung, gated on something the addon cannot see: a two-person party in which both members share a job. Party composition is not in any packet this reads, so step 2 has no evidence and the ladder simply waits there. 'Quest Reqs: Level 10 and up' is a level gate for ANY job, so jobs stays empty -- reading it as a job gate would lock this to one job forever. Fame 'S' is BG Wiki's San d'Oria shorthand and resolves.

steps.note: out through (C-7) in Northern San d'Oria; you arrive in a watchtower and he is straight ahead
you and one other player, both the same job, in a party of two -- nothing observable reports that

notes:
One bullet holding an OR across two zones. The Start field is empty, so the giver comes out of the walkthrough, and the walkthrough offers a choice rather than a sequence: the Audience Chamber in Ru'Lude Gardens OR the Bulwark Gate in Sauromugue Champaign (S). A single zone per step is a hard rule, so it becomes two steps sharing a group -- which is not literally what a group means (an unordered set is normally 'do all of them'), but it is what the player needs: both draw at once and either one finishes the quest. Neither is observable, so nothing can ever retire the wrong half; the quest closing does. Both entities are real and already known to this codebase -- v1's index marks 'audience chamber' at z=243 for TOAU 74, and the WotG mission pages examine the 'Bulwark Gate' in Sauromugue Champaign (S) repeatedly -- so neither is a name I invented. Grids are left null because THIS page gives none; other pages put the chamber at (H-6) and the gate at (E-6)/(F-6). Start records the Ru'Lude Gardens half, which is the one both the Description and the bullet name first. This header has no Fame line at all, hence the doubly-empty raw.

notes: Empty Start field again, and again the walkthrough supplies the giver -- but here it is an object, not an NPC: you click a Veridical Conflux. Cait Sith is named only in the Description as who wants to talk to you; he is a cutscene and gets no step, exactly the trap the Summoner AF pages set. The travel half of bullet 1 is not a separate rung -- the examine step already sits in Pashhow Marshlands (S), and a travel step to the zone you are already marking is a wasted rung. 'Veridical Conflux' is the form BG Wiki uses in all 110 mentions across the mirrored corpus, with no numeric suffix, and the (S) zone form resolves to 90. Grid (J-9) is the page's, given as being near the Pashhow gate crystal. There is nothing to hand in: the cutscene ends this quest and opens The Truth Is Out There, so no turn-in rung is invented.

steps.note: near the Pashhow gate crystal. The cutscene both ends this quest and begins the next, so this rung is the whole quest.

notes: Bullet 2 earns a rung where 'Out of One's Shell' bullet 2 did not, and the difference is that this one NAMES things: Onyx Quadav and Greater Quadav, in Palborough Mines. That is two real mob markers and a real place, so the obtain step is worth having; the auction-house alternative is recorded in the note rather than pretending the zone is optional. Its evidence is holding one Silver Name Tag, and step 3 only uses that tag as a requirement, so no item is evidence twice. Bullet 3 is not a step -- it is the reason the count is one: the tags are Rare, so you cannot carry two and the ladder can never ask for more. It merges into the trade with bullet 4. Repeatable Yes is kept; the reward is gil, which is not evidence of anything.
